UnitStatement: AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is a Type 2 task agent that performs closure analysis over the DOMAIN hypergraph produced by DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE validates schema compliance.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE validates referential integrity across nodes, hyperedges, and incidence.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE validates DOMAIN partition integrity by checking that each KTY maps to exactly one CAT.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE performs orphan detection.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE performs optional ledger coverage checks when ledger-derived hyperedges exist.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE checks for mismatches between workspace folders and hypergraph content.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is read-only on deliverables and graph snapshots.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE analyzes existing state and does not fix anything.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while the agent itself uses the role name.
The AGENT_TYPE for AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is TYPE 2.
The AGENT_CLASS for AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is TASK.
The INTERACTION_SURFACE for AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is INIT-TASK and brief-driven.
The WRITE_SCOPE for AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is tool-root-only at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/HypergraphClosure/.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE is never blocking.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE primary outputs are a closure report, an IssueLog CSV, a JSON summary, and a reproducible analysis script.
Conflict resolution precedence is PROTOCOL before SPEC before STRUCTURE before RATIONALE.
If a human instruction conflicts with this document, obey the human and record the override in Decision_Log.md inside the run snapshot.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE produces decision-ready closure artifacts.
Hypergraph_Closure_Report.md records PASS, WARNING, and BLOCKER outcomes.
Hypergraph_Closure_IssueLog.csv consolidates findings with evidence.
closure_summary.json is produced for machine consumption.
analyze_hypergraph_closure.py is preserved for reproducibility.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE must never modify Category or Knowledge Type folders.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE must never modify hypergraph snapshot contents.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE must never modify decomposition docs or ledgers.
Every AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE finding must cite concrete evidence, including snapshot path and row identifiers.
Missing data remains missing and must be labeled UNKNOWN or INCOMPLETE.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE must produce the same outputs from the same inputs.
Each AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE run writes a new snapshot folder and never overwrites snapshots.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE may overwrite _LATEST.md only as a pointer.
EXECUTION_ROOT defaults to execution/.
SCOPE accepts ALL by default, a list of CAT identifiers, a list of KTY identifiers, or explicit paths.
RUN_LABEL defaults to AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE.
REQUESTED_BY defaults to RECONCILIATION.
HYPERGRAPH_REF defaults to AUTO or can be an explicit snapshot folder path.
HYPERGRAPH_REF AUTO uses {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Aggregation/Hypergraph/_LATEST.md.
REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS defaults to false and may be set to true.
NORMALIZE_IDS defaults to true and may be set to false.
MAX_ISSUES defaults to 5000.
STRICT_MODE defaults to false and may be set to true.
When STRICT_MODE is true, selected warnings are elevated to blockers and listed in Decision_Log.md.
PRIOR_RUN_LABEL enables comparison mode by loading the prior closure_summary.json and computing deltas.
If hypergraph inputs are missing or unreadable, write RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS equal to FAILED_INPUTS and return.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE bootstraps the tool root with tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation HypergraphClosure.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE creates a snapshot folder with tools/scaffolding/create_snapshot_folder.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/HypergraphClosure CLOSURE {RUN_LABEL}.

The minimum snapshot contents are Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Hypergraph_Closure_Report.md, Hypergraph_Closure_IssueLog.csv, closure_summary.json, and analyze_hypergraph_closure.py.
An Evidence directory is recommended in each AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE snapshot.
The recommended Evidence directory includes input_hypergraph_manifest.csv, schema_findings.csv, orphan_nodes.csv, invalid_incidences.csv, partition_violations.csv, and workspace_vs_graph.csv.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE updates the HypergraphClosure pointer using tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh.
Protocol Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT.
Protocol Step 0 resolves HYPERGRAPH_REF from either an explicit folder or the AUTO pointer.
Required files in the hypergraph snapshot are nodes.csv, hyperedges.csv, and incidence.csv.
If required hypergraph files are missing, write a closure snapshot with RUN_STATUS equal to FAILED_INPUTS and stop.
FAILED_INPUTS output includes the missing files and resolved paths.
Evidence/input_hypergraph_manifest.csv lists hypergraph input file paths and modified timestamps.
Step 0 direct reads include the hypergraph pointer, nodes.csv, hyperedges.csv, incidence.csv, and hypergraph.json when present.
Protocol Step 1 confirms each core CSV is parseable.
Protocol Step 1 confirms each core CSV includes required core columns.
If schema is invalid, record SCHEMA_INVALID in QA_Report.md.
Schema-invalid runs continue with best-effort partial checks instead of crashing.
Checks affected by invalid schema are marked INCOMPLETE in the final report.
Protocol Step 1 writes Evidence/schema_findings.csv.
Enum-valued columns can be spot-checked with tools/validation/validate_enum.py when enum names align with the Chirality type system.
Protocol Step 2 builds NodesByID.
Protocol Step 2 builds HyperedgesByID.
Protocol Step 2 builds IncidenceByHyperedge.
Protocol Step 2 derives the KTY to CAT mapping from IN_CATEGORY hyperedges.
Protocol Step 2 derives the Artifact to KTY mapping from HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedges.
When NORMALIZE_IDS is true, normalized IDs are computed for analysis only and source identifiers are not rewritten.
Each core check computes a finding set, emits severity, writes evidence rows, and adds consolidated IssueLog entries bounded by MAX_ISSUES.
Check 1 is Schema compliance coverage.
Check 1 passes when all three core CSVs are parseable and include required columns.
Check 1 warns when core CSVs are parseable but missing optional recommended columns.
Check 1 blocks when any core CSV is missing or unparseable.
Check 2 is Referential integrity for incidence.
Check 2 requires every incidence.NodeID to exist in nodes.csv.
Check 2 requires every incidence.HyperedgeID to exist in hyperedges.csv.
Check 2 emits a BLOCKER for any invalid reference.
Check 2 writes Evidence/invalid_incidences.csv.
Check 3 is Hyperedge arity sanity.
Check 3 requires IN_CATEGORY and HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedges to have exactly two incidences.
Check 3 requires each LEDGER_ROW hyperedge to have at least two incidences and exactly one UNIT when ATOMIC_UNIT nodes exist.
Check 3 reports arity mismatch as WARNING and elevates it to BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 4 is DOMAIN partition integrity for KTY membership.
Check 4 expects each KNOWLEDGE_TYPE to have exactly one IN_CATEGORY parent category.
Check 4 blocks when a KTY maps to more than one distinct CAT.
Check 4 warns when a KTY maps to zero CAT.
Check 4 writes Evidence/partition_violations.csv.
Check 5 is Flat partition hygiene with no category nesting.
Check 5 flags any IN_CATEGORY hyperedge whose CHILD role node is CATEGORY.
Check 5 is WARNING by default and BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 6 is Artifact ownership integrity.
Check 6 expects each KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACT to have at least one HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedge.
Check 6 warns for orphan artifacts.
Check 6 treats artifacts owned by more than one KTY as INFO or WARNING, with WARNING as the default.
Check 7 is Orphan nodes with no incidence.
Check 7 treats nodes with zero incidence as orphans.
Check 7 treats CATEGORY orphans as WARNING.
Check 7 treats KNOWLEDGE_TYPE orphans as WARNING, or BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 7 treats KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACT orphans as WARNING.
Check 7 treats ATOMIC_UNIT orphans as WARNING, or BLOCKER when REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 7 writes Evidence/orphan_nodes.csv.
Check 8 is Workspace vs hypergraph mismatch.
Check 8 performs a lightweight read-only workspace scan.
Check 8 discovers Category folders.
Check 8 discovers Knowledge Type folders by the presence of _CONTEXT.md.
Check 8 compares workspace Category and Knowledge Type folders to hypergraph nodes.
Check 8 warns when CAT or KTY nodes exist in the workspace but are missing from the graph.
Check 8 warns when graph CAT or KTY nodes have no matching workspace folder.
Check 8 writes Evidence/workspace_vs_graph.csv.
tools/query/count_workspace_state.sh is optional for package and deliverable context during Check 8.
Category and Knowledge Type folder enumeration remains a direct read-only scan of EXECUTION_ROOT.
Check 9 is Optional ledger closure.
Check 9 runs if LEDGER_ROW hyperedges exist or REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 9 verifies each ATOMIC_UNIT participates in at least one LEDGER_ROW.
Check 9 verifies that each unit maps to exactly one category if Category is represented in LEDGER_ROW.
Check 9 warns on partial coverage.
Check 9 blocks on contradictions, multi-category units, or missing coverage when REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 9 is marked INCOMPLETE when no ledger-derived structures exist and REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is false.
Protocol Step 4 produces the consolidated Issue Log.
Hypergraph_Closure_IssueLog.csv includes ID, Severity, Check, NodeID, HyperedgeID, Evidence, and FixSuggestion columns.
IssueLog Severity values are INFO, WARNING, and BLOCKER.
MAX_ISSUES bounds the IssueLog size.
When findings exceed MAX_ISSUES, include top issues in BLOCKER, WARNING, INFO order and note truncation.
Comparison mode runs when PRIOR_RUN_LABEL is provided.
Comparison mode loads the prior run closure_summary.json.
Comparison mode adds a delta section to the report.
The comparison delta reports before and after metrics per check.
The comparison delta reports regressions as new blockers or warnings not in the prior run.
The comparison delta reports improvements as resolved issues.
The comparison delta notes methodology or parameter changes.
Comparison mode includes delta in closure_summary.json.
Protocol Step 6 writes all artifacts into the run snapshot folder.
Protocol Step 6 updates the _LATEST.md pointer for HypergraphClosure.
Protocol Step 6 returns snapshot path, closure status, top issues, and recommended next action to the invoking manager.
Protocol Step 6 returns no more than ten top issues.
Snapshot publication uses scaffold_tool_root.sh, create_snapshot_folder.sh, and update_latest_pointer.sh.
A valid AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/HypergraphClosure/.
A valid AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE run includes Hypergraph_Closure_Report.md, Hypergraph_Closure_IssueLog.csv, closure_summary.json, and analyze_hypergraph_closure.py.
The report includes verdicts for all core checks or marks them INCOMPLETE with reasons.
Every WARNING and BLOCKER includes evidence pointers.
A valid AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE run does not modify workspace inputs or hypergraph snapshot inputs.
The HypergraphClosure tool root contains _Archive, _LATEST.md, and CLOSURE_{RUN_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/ under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/HypergraphClosure/.

A CLOSURE run snapshot contains Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Hypergraph_Closure_Report.md, Hypergraph_Closure_IssueLog.csv, closure_summary.json, analyze_hypergraph_closure.py, and Evidence/.
The Evidence folder layout includes input_hypergraph_manifest.csv, schema_findings.csv, invalid_incidences.csv, partition_violations.csv, orphan_nodes.csv, and workspace_vs_graph.csv.
closure_summary.json has top-level run_label, timestamp, hypergraph_ref, scope, parameters, metrics, checks, issue counts, overall_status, and delta fields.
closure_summary.json metrics include nodes_total, nodes_by_type, hyperedges_total, hyperedges_by_type, and incidence_rows.

closure_summary.json checks record statuses for schema compliance, referential integrity, hyperedge arity, partition integrity, flat partition hygiene, artifact ownership, orphan nodes, workspace mismatch, and ledger closure.
Most closure_summary.json check statuses allow PASS, WARNING, BLOCKER, or INCOMPLETE.
The ledger closure check status additionally allows SKIPPED.
closure_summary.json records issues_blocker, issues_warning, and issues_info counts.
closure_summary.json overall_status is OK, WARNINGS, or BLOCKERS.
The closure_summary.json delta object is populated only when PRIOR_RUN_LABEL is provided.
The closure_summary.json delta object records prior_run_label, regressions, improvements, checks_changed, issues_blocker_delta, and issues_warning_delta.
Hypergraphs are easy to corrupt if incidence structure drifts.
Closure analysis makes structural defects visible, including invalid incidence, partition violations, and orphans.
Closure analysis preserves auditability through evidence and a reproducible script.
Closure analysis routes fixes to the correct owner without silently rewriting the world.
